headline: This law lets certain nonprofits, tribes, and government employers pay half of their unemployment costs up front to ease COVID-19 cash flow strain.
what_it_does: The law allows certain governmental entities, federally recognized tribes, and nonprofit organizations to pay 50% of unemployment benefits up front into a state Unemployment Trust Fund, instead of the full amount that the Department of Labor's April 27, 2020 guidance required. The up-front payment can only be used to reduce unemployment payments caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. States may also choose to reimburse these employers or reduce the amounts they owe for weeks of unemployment after March 12, 2020 and before the law was enacted.

who_it_affects.how: They may pay 50% of their unemployment costs up front instead of the full amount under the earlier federal guidance.
